subject: Media Literacy
title: Law Enforcement and Digital Evidence
description: A quick, practical guide to Law Enforcement and Digital Evidence.

hook.text: Police used a suspect's Google location history to place him at a crime scene. He was actually at a nearby store.

buildup.text: Law enforcement increasingly relies on digital evidence — location data, search history, and communications records.

discovery.text: Geofence warrants request data on everyone near a crime scene, sweeping up innocent people alongside suspects.

twist.text: Digital evidence is often treated as infallible. But location data can be inaccurate and metadata can be misinterpreted.

climax.text: When police trust algorithms over alibis, innocent people get caught in digital dragnets.

punchline.text: Your phone says you were there. That doesn't mean you did it.

quiz.question: What is a geofence warrant?
options: A warrant for a specific person's data
A request for data on everyone near a crime scene, including innocent people
